mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by a notary public in Hong Kong; then Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. Consular legalization is not required because both Hong Kong and mainland China are parties to the Hague Apostille Convention. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and never chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Satisfactory Standing) of the Hong Kong Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by a notary public in Hong Kong; then Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. Consular legalization is not applicable. Apostille path only; no chain to consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for the WFOE Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by a notary public in Hong Kong; then Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. No consular legalization since Hong Kong and mainland China are Apostille Convention members. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized by a notary public in Hong Kong; then Hague Apostille by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR. Consular legalization not required and must not be chained after an apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued by the Hong Kong Shareholder's Bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and service providers (including Stripe) must be screened before incorporation and on an ongoing basis. Screening must cover the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; the UK OFSI Consolidated List; the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's list of politically exposed persons and terror financing communications; the PRC Ministry of Public Security and People's Bank of China control lists; and the World Bank and Asian Development Bank debarment lists. Politically exposed persons must include family members and close associates. Screening results must be time-stamped, retained as audit evidence, reviewed by the Money Laundering Reporting Officer, and refreshed immediately before any share transfer, director change, new bank account opening, or invoice flow commencement.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Pre-registration Portal of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the People's Republic of China
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the SAMR Provisions on Enterprise Name Administration, a WFOE's statutory Chinese name must follow a four-tier structure: (1) administrative division, (2) a distinctive trade name of at least two Chinese characters, (3) an industry or business scope characterization, and (4) the organizational form Co., Ltd. All characters must be standard modern Chinese; traditional characters and pinyin are not accepted for the registered name. The foreign shareholder's name may be phonetically transliterated, but the transliteration must be clearly distinguishable and cannot impersonate a recognized brand without permission. Any English or pinyin appended in parentheses is for cross-border recognition only and has no independent legal effect.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a name rejection, the applicant must file a written reconsideration with the SAMR registry that issued the rejection within 15 working days of the written notification, attaching the original rejection notice and legal grounds establishing that the name complies with the Provisions on Enterprise Name Administration. The registry must decide within 15 working days. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the next-higher SAMR within 60 days, or initiate an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within 6 months of the denial. Throughout the appeal, a revised name can be submitted simultaneously to avoid delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected for a WFOE in the ERP/CRM vertical cloud software sector. SAMR requires a fixed, concrete office address with a valid lease contract for the entire proposed term; the tax authority will cross-check the landlord's property tax records. Banks, when opening accounts for the WFOE, will require a site visit and reject any virtual or PO Box address. A government-supported registrable address in selected free trade zones, such as Qianhai or Lingang, may be acceptable only if it is a physical, gazetted shared-office address under a formal tenancy agreement; pure mailbox services are never acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Risk quantile: High, with a 70-85% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months after registration. Inspection checklist: (1) lease signed with property owner and stamped by the real estate bureau; (2) company nameplate visible at the registered entrance; (3) actual personnel or legitimate remote IT infrastructure; (4) business records, invoices, and statutory books available at the site; (5) fire and safety inspection certificate; (6) evidence of continuous office use, such as utility bills and internet service, not sub-metered to another entity; (7) consistency between the observed business operations and the registered business scope.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision, effective 1 July 2024), including the general corporate formation, registered capital, articles of association, legal representative, executive director and supervisory provisions; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 4 and 29; Regulations on Foreign Investment Information Reporting; and, solely for the Hong Kong corporate shareholder, Hong Kong Companies Ordinance Cap. 622.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Enterprise Registration Bureau of the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); for the Hong Kong shareholder's corporate-status certifying documents, the Hong Kong Companies Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Liability Company and the resulting Business License for Enterprise Legal Person issued with a Unified Social Credit Code.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement for an ISIC 6201 software and cloud WFOE. The registered capital is fixed in the Articles of Association and subscribed by the Hong Kong shareholder; under the 2023 PRC Company Law the subscription may be paid in installments but must be fully paid within five years from formation. Capital contribution may be cash or non-cash property, but non-cash property must be appraised and transferred to the Company. The capital amount must be reasonably related to actual business needs.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD (THE 'COMPANY'). WHEREAS, the Company is incorporated or is in the course of incorporation as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China; WHEREAS, the sole shareholder of the Company has executed the Articles of Association and initiated the formation process; WHEREAS, the board of directors is required to approve the share capital subscription, the banking authorization, the registered office adoption, and the statutory officer appointments. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. That the registered capital of the Company shall be the amount set forth in the Articles of Association. The board confirms and approves the subscription by the sole shareholder, and directs management to demand and receipt the capital contributions according to the contribution schedule in the Articles and the statutory five-year contribution deadline. No further shareholder approval is required for the initial subscription and call, except as required by the Foreign Investment Law and the foreign exchange rules. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. That the Company shall open RMB and foreign currency bank accounts with one or more licensed banks in the People's Republic of China. The legal representative, the general manager, and the chief financial officer shall be approved signatories. The legal representative, or in his absence the general manager, shall be authorized to sign account opening application forms, treasury mandates, signature cards, internet-banking authorizations, and any supporting resolutions. All bank documentation must be consistent with the Articles, the anti-money-laundering policies of the bank, and the SAFE direct-investment registration. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. That the registered office of the Company shall be the address stated in the Articles of Association and the lease agreement submitted to the market supervision authority. Management is authorized to file such address with SAMR, to place the Company name plate at that address in accordance with local regulations, and to use the registered address on its contracts, invoices, and public filings. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. That the following persons are appointed to the offices set out below, each to hold office until removed by shareholder resolution or resignation: [Name A] as Executive Director and Legal Representative; [Name B] as General Manager; [Name C] as Supervisor; and [Name D] as Chief Financial Officer. The Supervisor shall exercise the statutory supervision powers under the Company Law and shall not simultaneously serve as Executive Director or General Manager. 5. GENERAL GRANT OF AUTHORITY. That all officers and counsel are authorized to sign, notarize, apostille, file, and submit all notices, returns, certificates, bank forms, and government filings necessary to give effect to these resolutions, and to attend the local SAMR, tax, foreign exchange, and trade authorities on behalf of the Company. These resolutions may be executed in counterparts and take effect immediately; this written resolution constitutes valid and binding corporate action of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Declaration and Foreign Investment Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) enterprise name self-service online portal; Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) Foreign Investment Negative List reference.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Chinese and English company name through the local SAMR online enterprise name self-service portal after confirming, from the current Foreign Investment Access Negative List, that vertical software publication and cloud services, ISIC 6201, are not restricted or prohibited. The sole shareholder, if a Hong Kong corporate entity, must provide notarized evidence of legal existence. The system will produce a name pre-registration notice. This name notice must be kept for later incorporation filing. If the address or business scope includes special regulated words, the applicant must first obtain approval from the relevant industry regulator; for this software scope no such pre-approval is expected.
required_dossiers: Proposed Company Name Application Form (one to three Chinese-language alternatives)
Passport or equivalent identity certificate of the ultimate beneficial owner or sole shareholder
Notarized Certificate of Incumbency or Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Hong Kong Companies Registry for the corporate shareholder
Power of attorney executed by the sole shareholder appointing the local formation agent
Completed Foreign Investment Negative List representation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused because of identical or confusing similarity, revise the proposed name and resubmit within the preservation period; if the refusal is based on an input error, amend the application. If the negative-list screening flags a restricted boundary, narrow the business scope or, if necessary, use a restricted structure requiring foreign-investment approval; for this software scope no such approval is expected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Enterprise Registration Bureau of the local Municipal Market Supervision Administration (SAMR) counter or online integrated government service portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the Articles of Association, the shareholder resolution approving the Articles, and the legal representative appointment letter. File the completed Company Establishment Registration Application with SAMR, together with the lease certificate and landlord ownership documents. The business scope must be drafted to include computer software development, packaged software sales and subscription, cloud computing services, technical consulting, and ERP and CRM vertical systems. SAMR will review company type, registered capital, shareholder identity, legal representative eligibility, supervisor eligibility, and registered address. If all conditions are met, the Business License and Unified Social Credit Code are issued; the license becomes the legal foundation for all subsequent banking, tax, and operational steps.
required_dossiers: Company Establishment Registration Application (signed by the legal representative)
Articles of Association (executed by all shareholders)
Shareholder resolution or written consent approving the Articles
Identity certificates or passport copies of the legal representative, supervisor, and general manager
Lease contract for the registered office, landlord real estate ownership certificate, and lessor consent
Name pre-registration notice
Appointment letters for legal representative, supervisor, general manager, and chief financial officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SAMR registration is suspended on query, the applicant has the right to submit supplementary documents or correct signatures within the designated correction window; if the application is rejected in writing, the investor may seek administrative reconsideration from the next higher market supervision authority or institute administrative litigation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: MOFCOM Foreign Investment Information Reporting and SAFE Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) Foreign Investment Information Reporting platform; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through the designated domestic bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the first 30 days from issuance of the Business License, complete the foreign-investment information reporting obligation to the Ministry of Commerce. Also instruct the designated bank to conduct SAFE foreign exchange registration for direct investment, because the Hong Kong shareholder will remit equity subscription funds. The bank will open a foreign currency capital account and a separate RMB basic account; the capital account may only be used for registered capital remittances. The bank will monitor the authenticity and consistency of the remittance with the Articles and the FDI registration. After remittance, the accounts must be used for business purposes; all cross-border payments must comply with foreign exchange current-account rules.
required_dossiers: Business License (original)
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
FDI Information Reporting Form (completed online)
Articles of Association and share subscription and contribution schedule
SAFE FDI registration application forms completed by the bank
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening and signatory appointments
Hong Kong shareholder's Certificate of Good Standing or Certificate of Incumbency
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the FDI report is queried, access the MOFCOM reporting system and correct the data; if the bank's SAFE registration is suspended, provide the bank with a fresh board resolution and the shareholder's notarized corporate documents, or reapply through a different designated bank. Late filings may be accepted with written explanation but are at regulator discretion.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Seal Engraving, Tax Registration, Social Insurance, and Operational Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau seal engraving and archival filing window; State Taxation Administration (tax registration); local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; bank account opening officer.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After securing the Business License, arrange for the engraving of the company seal, financial seal, invoice seal, and legal representative seal at a licensed engraving shop, and submit the seal impressions to the Public Security Bureau for archival filing. Complete tax registration by linking the Unified Social Credit Code to the State Taxation Administration systems, selecting the appropriate tax types, and applying for general taxpayer status where needed to support VAT crediting for software services. Register the enterprise with social insurance and housing fund for staff. The banking mandate documents must be presented or notarized as required; thereafter the bank can issue the certificate of account opening and the company can invoice clients.
required_dossiers: Business License original and copies
Public Security Bureau seal engraving and archival filing forms
Legal representative identity document
Board resolution for bank signatory appointments
Tax registration forms and tax type election statement
Social insurance and housing fund registration forms
Office lease and rent invoice or receipt for the tax address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax, seal, or social insurance registration is suspended due to document mismatch, replace or notarize the defective document and resubmit; if the legal representative cannot appear, provide a notarized power of attorney. If the tax system shows data not synchronized, ask SAMR to re-sync the Unified Social Credit Code before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational Readiness Confirmation and Fire Safety Coordination for Office Premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local fire rescue authority for office fire safety inspection; local Public Security Bureau window; landlord or property management company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing software and cloud operations, verify that the leased office has obtained the landlord's fire safety acceptance certificate or its equivalent, and keep the fire-protection documentation on site. File any post-incorporation change notifications in SAMR if the scope or registered address is adjusted. For pure software service commencement, no civil-defense operating license or environmental assessment is required; however, maintain corporate governance records, board resolutions, shareholder registers, and accounting books available for annual reports and tax filings. Arrange fire safety training and evacuation drills for all employees in coordination with the landlord and local fire authorities.
required_dossiers: Landlord's fire safety certificate or fire safety acceptance inspection document
Civil defense and fire safety compliance documentation for the leased office
Updated corporate records and minute book
Employment registration forms and payroll procedure confirmation
Post-registration change forms, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a post-license inspection reveals fire-safety defects, coordinate with the landlord to carry out remedial works and obtain a re-inspection; if SAMR or tax authority posts a compliance query, cure within the statutory response period and provide an explanation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - ISIC 6201 is pure digital and cloud software publication; no municipal industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no statutory operating license, manufacturing permit, or industrial permit required for ERP and CRM vertical cloud software services.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no physical industrial establishment; a leased commercial office for a software and cloud company is outside the statutory EIA catalogue.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable / Exempt from statutory Environmental Impact Assessment; no full EIA report or environmental registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste, or point-source industrial emissions; only ordinary domestic office waste and municipal sewage from the leased premises, handled by municipal utility authorities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable to manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations. For the leased commercial office, the landlord must maintain the fire-safety acceptance certificate and fire-protection equipment in accordance with the Fire Protection Law; the WFOE shall coordinate fire safety training and evacuation drills under local fire-rescue authority jurisdiction. No civil-defense operating permit or industrial occupational clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China; tax filings and registrations are performed through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) online portal and the nationwide Electronic Invoice Service Platform operated by the STA's provincial/municipal tax service branches at the WFOE's domicile.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Stage A: Incorporate the WFOE with the Administration for Market Regulation; the AMR issues an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code, which automatically functions as the WFOE's taxpayer identification number for PRC tax purposes. Stage B: Within 30 calendar days of the business license issuance, the WFOE's legal representative or authorized tax agent must complete the supplementary tax registration through the STA Electronic Tax Bureau, confirm the resident enterprise tax status, designate a resident financial/accounting contact, and link the Unified Social Credit Code to the entity's tax account. Stage C: If the WFOE intends to issue special VAT invoices and claim input VAT credits, it must complete VAT general taxpayer registration under the VAT Implementing Rules; below the statutory turnover threshold the entity may elect small-scale taxpayer status. Stage D: For the non-resident Hong Kong parent, no separate standalone TIN is required if it has no permanent establishment in China; instead, the WFOE acts as withholding agent and files the non-resident enterprise withholding registration with the STA, and the Hong Kong parent obtains a non-resident enterprise taxpayer identity number through that withholding registration procedure when applying for treaty benefits or withholding tax reductions. Stage E: The Unified Social Credit Code must be integrated with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) records and, if physical exports are added to the ERP/CRM business, with the customs export registration code to support cross-border foreign exchange receipts and export VAT zero-rating substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The PRC WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise taxable on its worldwide income as a separate entity at the 25% corporate income tax rate; the Hong Kong parent is a separate non-resident corporate investor. For VAT purposes the WFOE defaults to general VAT taxpayer status when standardized annual taxable sales exceed the statutory threshold, or may elect small-scale taxpayer status below the threshold.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification: PRC tax law does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections. The only material election is VAT taxpayer status: an enterprise with annual standardized taxable sales not exceeding RMB 5,000,000 may elect small-scale VAT taxpayer treatment, but registration as a general VAT taxpayer is mandatory once the threshold is exceeded and, once elected or required, the general taxpayer status remains effective for the statutory period. There are no CIT pass-through elections available to a WFOE.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 of annual standardized taxable sales; exceeding this threshold triggers mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration. A WFOE may voluntarily register as a general VAT taxpayer below the threshold in order to recover input VAT on ERP/CRM cloud software development and operating costs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The WFOE must issue fully digitalized electronic invoices through the Electronic Invoice Service Platform of the State Taxation Administration, which is integrated with the Golden Tax System Phase IV. Each invoice is assigned a unified national invoice number and cryptographic digital signature in near real-time; there is no separate physical anti-fraud stamp. For special VAT invoices used to support input VAT credits, the buyer, invoicing party, amount and VAT amount must be validated/cleared through the platform. For cross-border zero-rated or VAT-exempt software services, the taxpayer must file the cross-border taxable service zero-rating/exemption record with transaction contracts, foreign exchange receipt evidence and offshore consumption documents attached through the Electronic Tax Bureau before or at the time of issuing the relevant invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical goods, zero-rated export VAT applies when goods physically leave mainland China through a customs clearance point, the exporter files an Export Goods Declaration Form, the goods are exported under the WFOE's customs registration, full transportation evidence is retained, and export proceeds are repatriated through a SAFE-monitored channel. For the WFOE's vertical ERP/CRM cloud services, cross-border software as a service, software maintenance and related information system services supplied to a Hong Kong or other non-resident overseas recipient are eligible for zero-rating or VAT exemption under the STA's cross-border taxable services measures when the service is provided to an overseas enterprise, the service is wholly consumed outside mainland China, the service contract is executed in writing, and payment is received in foreign currency from outside China. Services rendered to the overseas company's permanent establishment or branch located in mainland China, or services that relate to real estate, goods, or taxable activities physically located or performed in mainland China, are ineligible and remain subject to 6% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Goods: Customs Export Goods Declaration Form with electronic customs clearance record evidencing physical export from mainland China.
Goods: transport document proving physical movement, namely Bill of Lading, multimodal waybill, or air waybill.

Goods and services: bank-issued foreign exchange receipt certificate, including the Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank/SAFE export proceeds collection confirmation, showing the overseas purchaser remitted the export/service consideration.
Services: signed cross-border software subscription/SaaS agreement identifying the Hong Kong or other overseas recipient and the ERP/CRM services to be consumed outside mainland China.
Services: overseas service acceptance certificate, usage/server access logs, or the overseas client's written confirmation evidencing that the cloud software services were wholly consumed offshore.

Registration files: customs registration/export-record code if physical goods are exported, together with the SAFE export collection and payment verification records supporting the 180-day foreign exchange repatriation requirement.

Invoice evidence: the VAT invoice issued for the zero-rated or exempt transaction as generated through the Electronic Invoice Service Platform, with the approved zero-rating/exemption filing reference.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA has authority to conduct retrospective audits, including opening prior years where export zero-rating, VAT exemption, or input credit claims are suspect. If the zero-rated export claim or VAT exemption is denied due to false documentation, missing foreign exchange repatriation, diversion to domestic consumption, or lack of offshore substance, the taxpayer must repay the full VAT avoided or refunded, with daily late-payment surcharges of 0.05% of the overdue tax, plus administrative penalties ranging from 50% to 500% of the tax under the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Levying and Collection. Where forged Customs export declarations, fabricated service contracts, counterfeit foreign exchange receipts, or circular offshore schemes are used to obtain export VAT refunds, the case will be referred to Customs and Public Security authorities for criminal investigation, with fines and terms of imprisonment authorized under the Criminal Law for export tax refund fraud. In addition, SAFE may impose monetary penalties for failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory 180-day verification window, and the tax authority will claw back any related export tax refunds and VAT exemption benefits together with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC), with supervisory delegation to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for trade and balance-of-payments controls; the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) regulates the Hong Kong parent but does not grant convertibility relief to the mainland WFOE.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange-rate system under which current-account payments and receipts are convertible in principle, while capital-account transactions remain subject to prior registration, approval, or quota controls. For the WFOE, the distinction is operationally decisive. Software export and CRM-service invoices denominated in foreign currency are current-account proceeds and can be collected into a designated bank foreign-exchange settlement account without case-by-case approval, provided the transactions are accurately declared under SAFE trade-monitoring codes. Surplus foreign exchange may be retained or converted to RMB at the onshore market rate. Dividend and profit remittances to the Hong Kong parent also flow through the current account, but banks require audited financial statements, corporate income tax settlement certificates, and a board resolution declaring and allocating profits; any mismatch in these documents will halt payment. Registered capital injection from the Hong Kong parent is a capital-account inflow and requires an SAFE Foreign Direct Investment registration, a dedicated foreign-currency capital account, and compliance with the bank's capital-account payment rules. Conversion is permitted only against verified payment purposes, and arbitrary settlement or speculative conversion is prohibited. The Hong Kong jurisdiction imposes no exchange controls, but it cannot create a compliance shortcut for the mainland WFOE's SAFE-regulated treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export foreign-currency receipts must be repatriated to China within not more than 180 calendar days from the date of customs export declaration, unless SAFE approves an extension for documented exceptional circumstances. Mandatory conversion ratio: none; the WFOE may retain 100% of export proceeds in a designated foreign-currency settlement account or voluntarily convert any portion into RMB at the onshore exchange rate. Full remittance, bank crediting, and underlying trade-inspection records must be preserved for SAFE audit.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Currency Capital Account and RMB Basic Operational Settlement Account
FDI Foreign Currency Capital Account, RMB Basic Deposit Account, and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMI solutions such as programmatic wallet platforms, virtual IBAN issuers, and fintech payment gateways are not viable for the mainland WFOE's onshore treasury operations. They generally lack a PBOC banking license, do not hold CIPS/CNAPS clearing membership, and are legally prohibited from accepting deposits or maintaining RMB settlement accounts for a China-registered entity. The WFOE must therefore use a licensed domestic bank for all collection, payroll, tax, and SAFE-visible capital flows. An offshore EMI, if licensed in Hong Kong, may support the Hong Kong parent's ancillary receivables or FX conversion, but should never be used as a pass-through account for WFOE registered capital injection because the transaction would be stripped of its SAFE compliance trail. Viability rating: Low for WFOE onshore clearing; Limited, and strictly auxiliary, for the Hong Kong parent.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The legal representative or an explicitly appointed statutory director must appear physically in-branch for account opening, original-ID verification, chop/seal certification, and the mandatory KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted as a complete substitute; a notarized and legalized power of attorney may allow an authorized agent to handle documentation for signatories, but it does not waive the principal identity verification. Some banks permit a pre-screening video call, but the final onboarding must take place onshore at the designated branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable ultimate beneficial ownership of the Hong Kong parent due to interposed nominee shareholders, discretionary trusts, or bearer share structures in non-public registries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A signed ownership cascade chart covering every intermediate entity; the Hong Kong parent's register of shareholders and directors; any trust deed, letter of wishes, and trust registration excerpt; notarized passport and proof-of-residence documents for each UBO; sanctions and politically exposed person screening reports issued by an internationally recognized due-diligence provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered capital injection from a third-party lender or pooled corporate treasury rather than the declared overseas shareholder, creating source-of-funds ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements and audited bank confirmation for the remitting shareholder for the past two financial years; a board resolution of the Hong Kong parent authorizing the equity subscription; the share subscription agreement; an explicit source-of-funds disclosure letter; and the remitting bank's SWIFT reference showing funds originated from the named shareholder's account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly formed WFOE with no tangible business substance in the software/ERP/CRM vertical, increasing the perception of a shell or pass-through vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A commercial lease or title deed for the registered address; employee labor contracts, payroll slips, social-security records, and individual income-tax filings; the WFOE's business license and tax registration; current-period VAT and corporate income tax returns; executed client or channel agreements for the CRM/ERP platform; cloud-hosting and software-licensing invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Repeated high-value outbound service payments to related Hong Kong parties without transfer-pricing or economic-substance support, indicating profit stripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: An intercompany service agreement with detailed scope and fee methodology; transfer-pricing master file and local file for the WFOE; benchmark study supporting arm's-length pricing; invoices matched to time records or deliverables; HK tax returns and proof of substance for the related party; SAFE-declared underlying contracts and customs records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound funds from the Hong Kong parent must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 or equivalent ISO 20022 message with a clearly stated purpose code restricted to the SAFE Foreign Direct Investment capital-injection scope, such as equity registered capital contribution or the corresponding SAFE transaction-code category; under no circumstances may the remittance be characterized as a general trade or services payment. Prior to execution, the WFOE must complete the FDI Foreign-Investment Information Report with the local market-regulation authority and SAFE, obtain the capital-account opening confirmation from the designated domestic bank, and verify that the remitted amount does not exceed the registered capital schedule. The funds must be credited to the dedicated FDI Foreign Currency Capital Account, after which the bank performs foreign-exchange settlement under the payment-first conversion-later capital-account monitoring protocol. Once credited, a Chinese certified public accountant issues a capital verification certificate, which forms the basis for the bank to release the funds to operating RMB accounts and for the market-regulation authority to update the equity contribution records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound service and license payments, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 with full contract, invoice, withholding-tax certificate, and SAFE transaction declaration. For physical hardware purchases or on-premises software consignments, a Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) or Documentary Collection (DP/DA) can be used, although the cloud vertical will mostly rely on clean payments under direct agreements. CNY-denominated settlements to mainland or Hong Kong counterparts may clear through CIPS; in all outbound cases, the bank will verify tax payment before release and the WFOE should maintain a rolling SAFE trade-inspection file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts for genuine current-account and foreign-debt flows, with back-to-back underlying documents and maturity matched to the exposure; speculative forwards are prohibited.
Onshore foreign-exchange swap transactions combining spot and forward legs, used to manage short-term RMB/USD/HKD liquidity mismatch while maintaining SAFE documentation.
Cross-currency swap agreements for registered foreign-currency loans, capped by the approved foreign-debt quota and requiring SAFE registration before drawdown.

Offshore RMB non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) solely at the Hong Kong parent treasury level; not permissible as a hedging vehicle for the mainland WFOE's onshore books because the WFOE has no offshore NDF access under current SAFE rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Standard HK$105 annual fee remains payable. Late delivery fees: HK$870 if delivered more than 42 days but not more than 3 months after the anniversary; HK$1,740 if more than 3 months but not more than 6 months; HK$3,480 if more than 6 months. Continued default is a ground for the Registrar to regard the company as not carrying on business and to initiate strike-off proceedings under section 746 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the expiry date shown on the current Business Registration Certificate; renewal notice is normally sent one month before expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal incurs a statutory late fee of HK$300 in addition to the registration fee and levy. Continuing failure to renew is an offence under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), punishable on conviction by a fine of up to HK$5,000 and imprisonment for one year, and supports a strike-off determination under section 746 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (BIR51) with audited financial statements, tax computation and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the issue date of the return, subject to IRD block extension arrangements for taxpayers with matched accounting dates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is an offence under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112); on conviction the maximum fine is HK$10,000 plus a further penalty up to three times the tax undercharged, and unpaid tax may attract a 5% or 10% surcharge depending on the default period. The IRD may issue estimated assessments and take collection and winding-up proceedings for persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (BIR56A) and annual IR56B remuneration forms
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the year of assessment ended 31 March, the return must be filed not later than 1 May of the following year, or within one month of the issue date if issued later, unless an extension is granted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing and false particulars are punishable under the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112); maximum fine on conviction is up to HK$10,000 per charge, with further penalties for incorrect or incomplete remuneration details. Continuing defaults may lead to prosecution and additional fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Compulsory for all Hong Kong incorporated private companies limited by shares regardless of turnover, balance-sheet size, or employee headcount. There are no quantitative audit exemptions under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). The only exemption is a dormant company with no significant accounting transactions that passes a valid special resolution to exempt the audit, provided it is not a banking company, insurance company, licensed corporation, or trustee company; the resolution must be delivered to the Companies Registry.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants; HKFRS are substantially aligned with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). Eligible private entities may elect to apply HKFRS for Private Entities, the simplified SME-style framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO filing exists in Hong Kong. The company must maintain a Significant Controllers Register (SCR) at a prescribed place in Hong Kong, usually the registered office, and must update it within 7 days of any change in significant controllers. Share transfers are recorded in the Register of Members; the Annual Return (NAR1) provides the statutory annual confirmation of members and company particulars at the anniversary date. Allotment returns must be filed with the Companies Registry within 1 month of allotment, and changes of directors or company secretary particulars must be filed within 15 days. There is no 30-day share-transfer reporting window under Hong Kong law.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,500 per annum for registered office and corporate secretarial agent services in Hong Kong
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 10,000 per annum depending on transaction volume, deferred revenue complexity under HKFRS 15, and the number of group entities requiring consolidation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: China levies a standard 25% corporate income tax (CIT). The effective rate may be reduced to 15% for a High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) under Article 28 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, to 20% (with a highly compressed base producing an effective rate around 5% for taxable income up to RMB 3 million) for Small Low-Profit Enterprises, and to 10% for key integrated circuit or software enterprises designated by the State. Eligible newly established software enterprises may also enjoy a 'two-year exemption, three-year 50% reduction' CIT holiday. An additional 100% super-deduction is available for qualifying R&D expenditures. Losses may generally be carried forward five years, extended to ten years for HNTE and Small Low-Profit Enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return Form A (Form A100000) and the supporting schedules A000000/A100000/A105000/A107041 etc., filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration's Jin San e-Taxation portal, either directly or through a licensed tax agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT returns and prepayments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter; the annual final CIT return and settlement must be filed within 5 calendar months after the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year WFOE, the annual deadline is 31 May of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross operating revenue from China-source ERP/CRM vertical cloud software, SaaS subscriptions, implementation, consulting and maintenance services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter all revenue attributable to Chinese customers and users on a gross basis, including subscription fees collected through Stripe Billing or direct debit. If payments are routed to a Hong Kong parent or group treasury account, do not omit them from the WFOE return merely because the contract is signed offshore. Apply the arm's-length standard to any intercompany allocation of subscription revenue, and recognise cloud subscription revenue over time under contract-liability accounting rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs and expenses: cloud infrastructure, hosting, data centre costs, subcontractor costs, employee compensation, amortisation of software/intangibles and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses supported by compliant Chinese invoices (including foreign-currency invoices or official tax receipts) and by actual service flows. Management fees and head-office charges paid to the Hong Kong parent are deductible only if genuine services are rendered, the charge is at arm's length and the recipient performs substantive functions; otherwise these are considered non-deductible transfers of profit. Royalties or service fees owed to the HK non-resident must be grossed up for China VAT and withholding tax before deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit before income tax computed under PRC accounting standards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile IFRS/HKFRS group accounting packages to PRC CAS. Include all accrued but unpaid intercompany royalties and interest, adjust for financing receivables and bad-debt provisions, and remove any revenue attributed offshore to the Hong Kong principal only where the related-party risk-return profile is supported by contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments, reflecting the adjusted accounting profit plus/minus all tax-adjustment items from Schedule A105000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back non-deductible entertainment fees above the statutory thresholds, administrative fines, excess intercompany management fees, unrealised cross-border FX losses and thin-capitalised interest under the 2:1 debt-to-equity safe harbour for related-party loans. Subtract R&D super-deductions, software enterprise incentive deductions, amortisation of acquired intangibles and tax-exempt income. For non-resident-linked structures, document the transfer-pricing adjustment on intercompany SaaS licensing, cloud processing fees and HK parent charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT computation at the headline 25% rate, then application of preferential rates, tax holidays and foreign tax credits to arrive at tax before withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the 15% HNTE rate or the software-enterprise two-year exemption/three-year 50% reduction only if the WFOE's R&D activity, software ownership and core business meet the statutory conditions. Attach the required schedules proving qualification. Where the HK parent has invoiced services or charged royalties, attach evidence that the HK entity is the beneficial owner and has economic substance; otherwise the tax authority may recharacterise and deny treaty benefits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net CIT payable or refundable after quarterly prepayments, together with any corresponding outbound withholding tax schedule for dividends, interest and royalties paid to the Hong Kong non-resident shareholder.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile quarterly prepayments to final liability. If a dividend distribution to the Hong Kong parent is declared or economically repatriated, ensure the WFOE as withholding agent reports the distribution and withholds at 10% unless the 5% treaty reduction is supported by a valid Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership declaration. Under-withholding or late remittance exposes the WFOE to withholding-agent penalties and daily late-payment interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return is penalised under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Administration Law with a RMB 2,000 fine, extending to RMB 2,000-10,000 for serious cases, plus a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on any unpaid tax. A false or fraudulent return under Article 63 attracts a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax plus daily surcharge and interest. If the tax evaded exceeds RMB 100,000 and constitutes more than 10% of the tax payable, the case is referred for criminal liability under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law, with imprisonment up to seven years in aggravated cases and additional monetary fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory PRC dividend withholding on outbound distributions to a non-resident company; reduced to 5% under the Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement where the Hong Kong shareholder directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE's capital and is the beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief: (1) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate from the Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department, evidencing that the shareholder is a Hong Kong resident company; (2) execute and file a beneficial-ownership declaration supported by organisational chart, board minutes, employment records, office premises, bank statements and commercial contracts showing real economic substance in Hong Kong; (3) ensure the Hong Kong company is not a conduit or nominee and has not entered a synthetic arrangement designed to funnel dividends to third-country residents; (4) submit the certificate package to the Chinese withholding agent before the distribution date, and retain a contemporaneous treaty-claim file. Where treaty benefits are denied because beneficial ownership is absent, the WFOE must withhold at 10%, and late or short withholding triggers penalties, surcharge and the possible assertion of a deemed distribution by the PRC tax authority.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory PRC CIT withholding is 10% on gross royalties and 10% on gross interest paid to a non-resident related party, in addition to VAT on imported services (generally 6% for software/royalty services with the corresponding input credit). Under the Mainland-Hong Kong arrangement, treaty relief is available at 5% for royalties and 7% for interest provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and satisfies the substantive-activities and anti-abuse clauses. Characterisation risk is significant: bundled software-as-a-service, technical assistance and cloud support fees may be recharacterised from royalties to service income, potentially altering both VAT and CIT treatment and the availability of treaty benefits.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB-denominated contemporaneous documentation thresholds under Public Notice 2016 No.42: Local File preparation is mandatory where annual related-party tangible-property transactions exceed RMB 200 million; intangible-property transfers exceed RMB 100 million; related-party service transactions exceed RMB 100 million; related-party financial transactions (loans, guarantees, advances) exceed RMB 100 million; or total other related-party transactions exceed RMB 40 million. Master File preparation is required where the consolidated group's annual related-party revenue exceeds RMB 1 billion or the group otherwise meets the published threshold. Documentation must be prepared in Chinese and submitted to the tax authority upon request or within the prescribed period after the annual CIT filing.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The structure must satisfy the Economic Substance Regulations doctrine and the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) test. The Hong Kong parent cannot simply hold legal title to Chinese-developed software, ring-fence invoices, or collect dividends without local decision-making, employees, offices, bank accounts and risk management in Hong Kong. The Chinese WFOE must retain or compensate for the functions actually performed in China: software development, cloud hosting, customer contracting, implementation and support. If the Hong Kong company is a shell or the arrangement has no genuine business purpose, the PRC tax authority may disregard the legal form, recharacterise the Hong Kong entity as a hybrid branch, assert a permanent establishment in China, or apply the Principal Purpose Test to deny treaty benefits. For Hong Kong tax purposes, extraterritorially sourced income may be non-taxable, but only where substantive economic activities are carried on in Hong Kong; passive royalty or dividend holding without CIGA undermines both treaty claims and Hong Kong residence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording Chinese ERP/CRM cloud subscription revenue in a Hong Kong or offshore bank account, using Stripe Billing or direct-debit rails outside the WFOE's China entity, issuing no Chinese VAT/CIT invoice, and omitting the China-source revenue from the WFOE's corporate income tax return while simultaneously deducting intercompany royalties or management fees paid to the shell Hong Kong parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the PRC Tax Administration Law: recovery of the underpaid tax, daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05%, and a penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law: criminal tax-evasion liability where the amount evaded exceeds RMB 100,000 and exceeds 10% of the tax payable, carrying up to three years' imprisonment for ordinary cases and up to seven years plus fines for large amounts with a high proportion of evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false returns or authorise offshore routing can be made personally liable through veil-piercing orders for the recovery of unpaid tax, interest and penalties, with civil asset restitution from personal and family assets. They will also be placed on the exit-control/blacklisting system, preventing departure from China until the tax debt is settled; in fraud cases, criminal imprisonment of up to seven years may be imposed on the responsible director or de facto controller.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering via Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring customer receipts so that Chinese users pay via offshore Stripe Billing or direct debit into a Hong Kong or third-country account, without the WFOE registering for VAT, issuing Chinese fiscal invoices, or reporting the revenue; commingling recovered subscription income with personal assets; using back-to-back management fees, royalties or fake intercompany loans to launder the proceeds of unreported tax evasion through the banking system.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 191 of the PRC Criminal Law criminalises money laundering of the proceeds of tax crimes, with imprisonment from five up to ten years and confiscation of assets for aggravated cases. The PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law obligates the payment institution, the WFOE and its directors to implement customer due diligence and suspicious-transaction reporting; violations attract administrative fines up to RMB 5 million for institutions and personal fines for responsible individuals, together with suspension of payment licences or disqualification of directors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto officers who design or benefit from offshore collection schemes are personally exposed to frozen bank accounts, seizure of property, joint and several civil restitution to the tax authority, exit-control blacklisting and travel bans while proceedings are pending. In criminal AML cases, imprisonment of up to ten years may be imposed, and the corporate veil will be pierced if the WFOE is shown to be a façade used to carry out illicit money flows.
